Title: Successful login with valid credentials
Preconditions: User has a registered account. System is accessible.
Steps: Navigate to the login page. | Enter a valid registered email address. | Enter the correct password. | Click the "Login" button.
Expected Result: User is authenticated and redirected to the dashboard. Session is established.

Title: Happy path: The email field is required and must follow a valid email format
Preconditions: System is in the expected initial state. All dependencies are available.
Steps: Set up the preconditions as described. | Perform the action described by: "The email field is required and must follow a valid email format (e.g., user@example.com)." | Observe the system response.
Test Data: Valid inputs meeting all stated requirements.
Expected Result: System behaves as specified: The email field is required and must follow a valid email format (e.g., user@example.com)..

Title: Happy path: The password field is required and must be at least 8 characters
Preconditions: System is in the expected initial state. All dependencies are available.
Steps: Set up the preconditions as described. | Perform the action described by: "The password field is required and must be at least 8 characters long." | Observe the system response.
Test Data: Valid inputs meeting all stated requirements.
Expected Result: System behaves as specified: The password field is required and must be at least 8 characters long..

Title: Login with incorrect password
Preconditions: Valid user account exists.
Steps: Navigate to the login page. | Enter a valid email address. | Enter an incorrect password. | Click Login.
Expected Result: Login is rejected. An error message is displayed (e.g. "Invalid credentials"). User remains on the login page.

Title: Login with non-existent email
Preconditions: System is accessible.
Steps: Navigate to the login page. | Enter an email not registered in the system. | Enter any password. | Click Login.
Expected Result: Login fails. A generic error message is shown. The system does not confirm or deny account existence.

Title: Submit with invalid email format
Preconditions: Form is displayed.
Steps: Focus on the email field. | Enter a value in an invalid format. | Attempt to submit.
Expected Result: Form submission is prevented. Inline validation error states the email format is invalid.

Title: Submit form with all required fields empty
Preconditions: Form is displayed and all fields are empty.
Steps: Leave all fields blank. | Click the submit button.
Expected Result: Submission is blocked. Validation errors are shown for each required field.

Title: Password exactly at minimum length (8 characters)
Preconditions: Registration or password change form is accessible.
Steps: Enter a password of exactly 8 characters. | Submit the form.
Expected Result: Password is accepted. The system treats 8 characters as a valid minimum.

Title: Password one character below minimum (7 characters)
Preconditions: Form is accessible.
Steps: Enter a password of exactly 7 characters. | Submit the form.
Expected Result: Password is rejected. Error message indicates the minimum length is 8 characters.

Title: Account lockout at exactly 5 failed attempts
Preconditions: Valid user account exists. No prior failed attempts.
Steps: Perform 4 failed login attempts. | Attempt one more login with wrong credentials.
Expected Result: Account is locked on the 5th attempt. A lockout message is displayed.

Title: Verify 4 failed attempts does NOT lock the account
Preconditions: Valid user account exists. No prior failed attempts.
Steps: Perform 4 failed login attempts. | Attempt login with the correct password.
Expected Result: Account is not locked. Login succeeds on the 5th attempt using correct credentials.

Title: Session expires exactly at 30-day boundary
Preconditions: "Remember Me" was checked at login.
Steps: Simulate time advancing to exactly 30 days after login. | Attempt to access a protected page.
Expected Result: Session expires. User is redirected to the login page.

Title: Login with leading/trailing spaces in email
Preconditions: Valid user account exists.
Steps: Enter email with a leading or trailing space (e.g. " user@example.com"). | Enter correct password. | Submit.
Expected Result: System trims whitespace and processes the login, OR displays an appropriate validation error.

Title: Login with email in mixed case
Preconditions: User account was registered with a lowercase email.
Steps: Enter the registered email in mixed case (e.g. USER@EXAMPLE.COM). | Enter the correct password. | Submit.
Expected Result: Login succeeds. Email comparison is case-insensitive.

Title: Password containing special characters and Unicode
Preconditions: Registration form is accessible.
Steps: Enter a password with special characters and/or non-ASCII characters. | Submit.
Expected Result: Password is accepted and stored securely. No truncation or encoding errors occur.

Title: Submit form by pressing Enter key
Preconditions: Form is displayed with data entered.
Steps: Fill in valid form data. | Press the Enter key instead of clicking Submit.
Expected Result: Form is submitted via the Enter key. Behaviour is identical to clicking the submit button.

Title: Double-click the submit button rapidly
Preconditions: Valid form data is entered.
Steps: Double-click the submit button in quick succession.
Expected Result: The action is processed only once. No duplicate submissions or errors occur.

Title: Behaviour when session expires mid-interaction
Preconditions: User is authenticated and on a form or page.
Steps: Allow the user session to expire (simulate timeout). | Attempt to perform an action or submit data.
Expected Result: User is redirected to the login page. A message informs the user the session has expired. No data is lost silently.

Title: Page refresh during an ongoing operation
Preconditions: User has started an operation (e.g. uploading, submitting).
Steps: Initiate the operation. | Immediately refresh the browser page.
Expected Result: System handles the refresh gracefully. Either the action completes or the user is informed they need to retry.

Title: Email field accepts only valid format
Preconditions: Form containing an email field is displayed.
Steps: Enter each invalid format listed in test data. | Attempt to submit after each entry.
Expected Result: Each invalid format triggers an inline validation error. The form is not submitted.

Title: Password field enforces 8-character minimum
Preconditions: Password input field is visible.
Steps: Enter a password shorter than 8 characters. | Attempt to submit.
Expected Result: Validation error: "Password must be at least 8 characters." Form is not submitted.

Title: Required fields display errors when left blank
Preconditions: Form is displayed.
Steps: Leave all detected required fields empty. | Click the submit button.
Test Data: Required fields: email field, password field
Expected Result: All required fields are highlighted. Specific validation messages appear for each field.

Title: Input fields enforce character type restrictions
Preconditions: Form is accessible.
Steps: Identify fields with type restrictions (numeric, alpha, etc.). | Enter values violating the type constraint. | Submit.
Test Data: Cross-type inputs: numbers in text-only fields, text in numeric fields.
Expected Result: Inappropriate character types are rejected with informative validation messages.

Title: Locked account message after 5 failed attempts
Preconditions: Account lockout has been triggered.
Steps: Perform 5 consecutive failed login attempts. | View the displayed message.
Expected Result: Account is locked. Message clearly states the account is locked and provides instructions (e.g. contact support or wait).

Title: Attempt login on a locked account
Preconditions: Account is already locked after 5 failed attempts.
Steps: Attempt to log in with valid credentials on a locked account.
Expected Result: Login is blocked. Locked account message is shown. User is NOT logged in even with correct credentials.

Title: System handles server error (HTTP 500) gracefully
Preconditions: Server is configured to return a 500 error for this request (test environment).
Steps: Perform a standard action (e.g. submit a form, load a page). | Observe the error response.
Expected Result: A user-friendly error message is displayed. No raw stack traces or technical details are exposed to the user.

Title: Network timeout during form submission
Preconditions: Network is throttled or disabled in developer tools.
Steps: Fill in valid form data. | Submit the form. | Observe behaviour when the network times out.
Expected Result: A timeout error message is shown. The user can retry. No partial or corrupt data is saved.

Title: Error messages do not reveal sensitive system information
Preconditions: Various error conditions are triggered.
Steps: Trigger validation errors, authentication failures, and server errors. | Examine all error messages.
Test Data: Invalid inputs, wrong credentials, network failures.
Expected Result: Error messages are informative for the user but do not expose internal paths, database details, stack traces, or user data.
